Friday was a SHARP, DISTINCT escalation, not a simple continuation of Thursday's Fed/Philly-Fed risk-off: S&P 500 -3.70% to 6910.39 (5th straight down day, confirming a correction from October highs), Nasdaq -5.28%, Russell 2000 -2.76%, VIX +26.2% to 35.89 (highest since March). The proximate triggers were two Friday-specific AI-credibility shocks -- Reuters reported SEC enforcement staff are examining Nvidia's accounting practices (NVDA -14%, ~$500bn of market cap erased) and Ming-Chi Kuo reported Alphabet cut ~20% of its 2027 Broadcom-designed TPU orders in favor of MediaTek (AVGO -11.4%, MRVL -10%) -- landing on monthly options expiration day when ~55-57% of SPY/QQQ's negative gamma was rolling off, a structural amplifier that helps explain why VIX moved so much more than the index itself. Gold and silver fell in the SAME session as equities (GLD -3.67%, SLV -6.74%, GDX -5.00%, SILJ -5.89%) despite softer US data (final UoM sentiment rose to 51.5, inflation expectations fell to 3.7%/3.3%) -- analysts attribute this to a margin-call transmission mechanism (leveraged investors raising cash from liquid winners to meet equity-related calls) rather than a fresh metals-specific catalyst, consistent with COMEX managed-money futures positions shrinking even as ETF holdings rose. Rare earths gave back their 3-day rally (MP -7.39%, having rallied Nov 17-19 on US-China trade-talk optimism and a 3-insider cluster buy) as broad-market beta overwhelmed the idiosyncratic story. Bitcoin extended a separate, multi-week decline (-4.51% to $59,109) tied to ~$1.9bn of cumulative spot-ETF outflows, MSCI's removal of Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes, and thin weekend Coinbase-concentrated selling -- this looks like continuation of an existing drain, not a new Friday-specific shock. CNN Fear & Greed fell to 14 (Extreme Fear, from 19 Thursday), yet counterintuitively BofA/EPFR and Lipper's week-ended-18-Nov fund flows (published Nov 20, finally covering this entire selloff week) both showed net equity INFLOWS (+$66.6bn and +$59.2bn respectively) -- a genuine divergence between price action and fund-level flows worth flagging rather than reconciling into one narrative. Fed Governor Waller's Nov 18 call for a 'shock therapy' 50bp December hike, reinforced by Governor Cook's hawkish tone Nov 20, keeps the rate backdrop a second, independent headwind. All 40 universe calls plus the 9-ticker rare-earth basket were re-levelled this run; the largest-magnitude-move tickers got fresh ticker-specific drivers, the rest were nudged in the direction of the broad shock per house rule rather than re-invented without a fresh catalyst.

macro.regime: Correction deepens into the weekend: a reinforced hawkish Fed chorus, a violent crypto round-trip, and widening AI-capex-credibility doubt compound Friday's Nvidia/Broadcom shock
macro.narrative: Friday 20 Nov's Nvidia SEC-accounting-probe and Broadcom/Google TPU-order-cut shock did not get walked back over the weekend -- if anything the read-through widened: BofA's Global Fund Manager Survey (published this weekend) showed the largest cut to tech positioning since June 2006, with 52% of managers now expecting an AI hyperscaler to announce a capex cut within six months, and reports surfaced of a separate US investigation into Singapore's Megaspeed International over alleged diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China. The Fed side also hardened rather than softened: Dallas Fed's Logan said she now favors two more rate hikes beyond December, reinforcing Waller's push for a 50bp 'shock therapy' move at the Dec 8-9 FOMC, with markets pricing a ~90-99% probability of at least a 25bp hike and essentially no probability of a cut. Crypto had a violent, largely self-contained round-trip: Bitcoin fell to roughly $55,100 (lowest since Sept 2024) on $2.4-2.7bn of liquidations before recovering to ~$59,900 by Sunday SGT morning -- net flat-to-up vs Friday but via a far more volatile path, with Ethereum underperforming. Partial counterweights exist: Friday's flight-to-quality bond bid was genuine (10y -12bp to 4.92%, TLT +2.6%), China's central bank extended a 24-month streak of gold purchases despite the price fall, and Beijing reconfirmed (not escalated) its rare-earth export-control suspension through Jan 10, 2027. As of this Sunday-morning SGT run, the open question -- whether Friday was a mechanically amplified single bad day (negative-gamma options expiry) or the start of a genuine AI-capex-cycle repricing -- remains unresolved, but the weekend's incremental evidence leans toward treating it as more durable than a one-day event.
